items.title: Document the stale-doc misclassification failure mode
items.context: Use the verified case: signature_backfill data was completed (656 backfilled signatures, commit 2750aadef), but an older plan-only document could still make a host think the task remained undone.
items.userSees: The execution plan contains a section named "Verified Failure Mode" with the Claude stale-plan incident, commit 2750aadef, 656 backfilled signatures, and the distinction between the plan-only document and the completed outcome record.

happy.desc: The new execution plan documents the stale-doc misclassification using the verified backfill case: plan-only doc, completed outcome doc, commit 2750aadef, and 656 backfilled signatures.

edge.desc: The failure-mode section distinguishes completed backfill data from the deferred causal/RCT parts of the Experience Layer record, so the plan does not overclaim that every experience-layer idea is complete.

adversarial.desc: The plan explicitly says hosts must not use old plan-only prose as proof that work is missing without checking current Lattice facts first.

verificationEvidence.note: Failure-mode section documents the verified stale-doc incident and proof anchor (commit 2750aadef, 656 signatures).
Plan-only status is explicitly separated from proof and causal completion context.

items.title: Define the truth-first host handoff contract
items.context: Specify that live Lattice state, DONE summaries, accepted outcome records, current code/data evidence, and fresh validation outrank stale planning prose. Hosts must not claim work is missing from a plan-only document alone.
items.userSees: The execution plan contains a section named "Truth-First Host Handoff Contract" listing the source priority order and the rule that hosts cannot tell the user work is missing from a plan-only document without checking live Lattice facts.

happy.desc: The plan defines a source priority order where current Lattice state, DONE summaries, accepted outcome records, code/data evidence, and fresh validation outrank stale plan prose.

edge.desc: The contract preserves dev-memory and learning hints as advisory context, not gate evidence or Authority/production proof.

adversarial.desc: The contract includes a fail-closed wording rule: if a host only has stale plan prose, it must say it needs to verify current facts rather than telling the user to redo the task.

items.title: Specify implementation stories and verification gates
items.context: Break the solution into concrete follow-up stories: document supersession metadata, handoff preflight fact pack, dev-memory preflight injection, and stale-plan warning/guardrail checks.
items.userSees: The execution plan contains a section named "Implementation Stories and Gates" with concrete follow-up stories for supersession metadata, handoff preflight fact packs, dev-memory injection, stale-plan warnings, and their verification commands.

happy.desc: The plan breaks the solution into concrete implementation stories with owner, scope, deliverables, and acceptance checks for each story.

edge.desc: The implementation plan handles historical/reference documents that should not be treated as stale active backlog, avoiding noisy false positives.

adversarial.desc: The verification gates include a negative case where an old plan-only document says future work, but current DONE summary/data evidence proves completion, and the host must not ask the user to redo it.
